rule_text:
The rule, fixed before any candidate ran (written 2026-11-14 into this docstring; `draw` copies it, with the constants
below and the sha256 of every frozen file, into selection.json before the first candidate runs):

1. Freeze. FROZEN below lists what decides an episode's layout and the reference program's run (verify.py, test.sh,
   grader_config.json, netguard.py, episode_trace.py, the hidden bench plan, the oracle token's sha256, the hidden kit's
   tarball tests/assets/gt.tar.xz, the solution's solve.sh / assemble.py / token) and FROZEN_TREES the code and models
   underneath (tests/arm, tests/common, tests/render, tests/render_filament, tests/room, the given robot models).
   `draw` records their sha256; every later command refuses to go on when one of them differs (the robot models are
   compared through the folder a run is given). The task's files were not committed when the set was selected,
   so the draw's UTC time and these hashes are the record of the freeze.
2. Draw. 12 candidates c00..c11 from os.urandom: seed = int.from_bytes(8 bytes, "little") % 2**63, drawn again while
   below 2**32 or equal to an earlier seed. Candidate i is in stratum STRATA[i % 4] (layout.STRATA: the stand's yaw sign
   x the stick pack's lead end: yaw+lead0, yaw+lead180, yaw-lead0, yaw-lead180) and round i // 4, so every stratum has
   three candidates in drawn order. selection.json is written before any candidate runs; `digests` then adds each
   candidate's layout digest (layout.layout_digest(layout.episode_layout(seed, plan, kit, cfg = grader_config["layout"],
   stratum)): a pure function of the inputs, no physics) and its layout draws (for the hollowing check).
3. Run. Every candidate runs ONCE in each of three environments, the privileged reference program exactly as the
   oracle plays it (one frame of each camera, then `reference_assemble`, then `finish`):
   - host: the development venv on the development machine, in-process: CarInfoServer(the kit unpacked from
     tests/assets/gt.tar.xz, the given robot models, the hidden bench plan, grader_config.json with the MuJoCo agent
     renderer, privileged) -> reset(seed, stratum) (its digest must be the recorded one) -> the episode trace of
     verify.py attached -> handle("get_camera" top), handle("get_camera" wrist), handle("reference_assemble"),
     handle("finish") -> finalize();
   - pod: the same on the second machine (another CPU: the shared cloud machine), its own interpreter and libraries;
   - image: the task image, through tests/test.sh -> verify.py with the solution/solve.sh submission (the oracle
     token) and the local kit tarball, one verify run per round (its four candidates are the set of that run); and,
     because verify keeps no frame, the top frame 0 of every candidate rendered once more in the same image by the
     agent renderer of grader_config.json (Filament) to measure what the top camera sees (`view`).
   All 12 candidates run in every environment, also those of a stratum whose earlier candidate passes (evidence for
   the hollowing check). A run that ends without a complete result because of the infrastructure (the process was
   killed, the machine or the container went away) is run again; a completed run is final.
4. Keep. A candidate passes one environment's run when: the layout digest is the recorded one; the reference program
   ran (no exception, its report reached finalize); all eight mates are LOCKED and the stage score is 1.0; its
   unplanned contacts are 0; the episode is hard_ok (no robot link above 30 N, no sustained part force above 150 N)
   and the largest sustained part force is below 150 N; at every capture of every mate the pose error is at most 50 %
   of that mate's capture window (reference.capture_ratios: the largest of lateral / window, tilt / window (a seat's
   total rotation) and, keyed, clock / window; the distance short of home is not an error: a unit is captured on its
   way in); every loose unit is at least 30 % seen in the top camera's frame 0 (4000 area-weighted
   samples on the unit's visual meshes; a sample is seen when it projects into the frame and the frame's sensor
   depth there is valid and within 15 mm of the sample's depth). A candidate passes when it passes in all three
   environments. A stratum's first passing candidate in drawn order is its episode; the episodes go into
   episodes.json in the order of STRATA.
5. Fallback. If a stratum has no passing candidate, no set is written and grader_config.json is not changed: the
   pre-written fallback (the oracle on the nominal layout, oracle_nominal_layout true, the agent still graded
   on a fixed hidden set) is written up as a recommendation for the maintainers.
6. Hollowing check (`report`). Flags: (a) more than 1/3 of the candidates dropped; (b) two or more drops share a cause
   (the same clause on the same mate or unit); (c) capture margin: per mate class (battery, deck, compute, lidar,
   wheel), the kept episodes' capture ratio (the largest of the three environments) against the dropped candidates':
   flagged when, on a class that dropped no candidate through its capture clause, the kept mean is below the dropped
   mean by more than 0.10 of the window (the dropped layouts were harder for the reference on mates that did not
   reject them); on a class that did drop candidates through its capture clause the gap is by construction and is
   reported, with each kept episode's place in the population of the earlier 100-seed campaign when one is given
   (`--population`); (d) the layout draws of the kept, the dropped and all candidates are reported (stand / clamp /
   shelf / tray offsets, the plays, the bench units' poses, the hubs' angles off the nearest hex orientation). A flag
   is reported with the set; the remedy is the precedent's (fix the reference program, freeze again, draw a new
   selection that supersedes this one), never knowingly keeping an easy subset.
7. Determinism record: per candidate and environment the mates' states, capture ratios and capture times, sim time,
   ticks, the largest forces, an outcome fingerprint (sha256 over finalize's physics fields without wall-clock
   values) and the sha256 of the episode trace's qpos (float32 every 4 ticks, verify's own recorder); host and pod also
   a sha256 of every control tick's qpos + qvel (float64). `determinism` writes the tables.
source: os.urandom: 8 bytes little-endian per seed mod 2**63, drawn again below 2**32 or on a repeat; candidate i -> stratum STRATA[i % 4], round i // 4 (0 seeds redrawn)
expectation: A priori, from the earlier 100-seed campaign of the same reference program (seeds 101-200, 25 per stratum, known hub clock: the final reference_shop.py is byte-identical in physics there): the battery's capture ratio exceeded 0.5 in 16 of 100 runs, all in the lead180 strata (yaw+lead180 10 / 25, yaw-lead180 6 / 25; lead0 at most 0.384); every other mate at most 0.049; 100 / 100 at 8 / 8 with 0 unplanned contacts and at most 13.2 N sustained. Expected: a lead0 stratum keeps its first candidate; a lead180 candidate drops with probability about 0.24-0.40 through the battery's capture clause; the chance that a lead180 stratum has no passing candidate of three is about 0.064 (yaw+lead180) and 0.014 (yaw-lead180), so about 0.08 that no set can be formed. Host and pod are different CPUs: the earlier campaign saw a one-tick drift from the third step on, which can move a capture ratio near 0.5 between environments. Visibility in the top frame: an earlier measurement found at least 40.8 % (the LiDAR) on 10 seeds.

pod: battery captured at 0.769 of its window (tilt)

amendments.authority: the lead designer's decision at the task's finalization (2026-11-15): amend the frozen-table rule of the hidden set with a dated amendment in the selection record before any file changes; no reselection, no redraw
amendments.amends: rule 1 (Freeze) of rule_text, as drawn at 2026-11-15T04:57:01Z
amendments.rule: Rule 1 as amended: the frozen table covers what determines an episode's outcome: the kit, the cell and layout code, the reference program, the server, verify and the grader's values. The publication metadata (the location and the hash of the hidden kit's archive) and the documents the agent reads are recorded by hash, but their change does not invalidate the set. In detail: (a) the hidden kit is frozen by its content, not by its archive's bytes: 'tests/assets/gt.tar.xz#members' = sha256 over the sorted lines '<member name> <sha256 of the member's bytes>' of the archive's file members; (b) tests/grader_config.json is frozen by its values: 'tests/grader_config.json#values' = sha256 of its canonical JSON (keys sorted, separators ',' and ':', ASCII) without hidden_gt.url, hidden_gt.sha256 and hidden_gt.note (the archive's location, its hash and the sentence that describes the location; verify never reads the note; hidden_gt.files, tries and backoff_s stay frozen); (c) every other file and tree of the draw's table stays frozen with its drawn sha256 (9 files, 6 trees); (d) recorded, never invalidating: the archive's sha256 and hidden_gt.url / sha256 / note (publication), and the files the agent reads or that are derived from them (instruction.md, environment/setup/payload/, environment/assets.sha256, environment/assets/payload/given/{parts, drawings, manual}/, environment/assets/payload/render/, tests/setup_payload/, tests/given_hashes.json); a later change of them is entered in recorded_changes with its date and reason. Files outside both tables stay outside the rule as before. The candidates, their runs, the set and tests/hidden/episodes.json stay as drawn.
amendments.why: the rule as drawn froze two files whose bytes carry more than an episode's outcome: grader_config.json also holds the hidden kit archive's download location (a placeholder revision until the owner approves the upload) and tests/assets/gt.tar.xz is frozen by its archive bytes; publishing the kit (filling in the revision, or re-packing the same members) would have invalidated a set whose episodes it cannot change. The documents the agent reads were in neither table; they are now recorded so that every text change stays traceable

amendments.why: the files that carry the limit are frozen as wholes: grader_config.json by its values, verify.py by its bytes, tests/arm as a tree; the new limit changes bytes in all three, yet a threshold of the watch enters no episode's physics or layout, only which contacts are recorded as violations. The selection's keep rule for the reference program (rule 4 as drawn: 8 / 8 in all three environments, no unplanned contact, the episode hard_ok with no robot link above 30 N and no sustained part force above 150 N, the largest sustained force below 150 N) used a robot-contact limit of 30 N, which is stricter than 150 N: every candidate that met it meets the new limit, every candidate keeps its outcome, and nothing is reselected; the reference program's robot links press on nothing in the recorded runs (0 N), so the set that the four episodes are, and every outcome the reference program reaches on them, stay valid under 150 N as under 30 N. The limit is one number (grader_config.json safety.robot_force_N), from which the cell's watch, describe(), cell_config.json and every agent-visible text take it; the cell's default (arm/assembly_car/cell.py) is the same number
